feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The encoding treats the passport as a conceptual and institutional artifact, not as a physical booklet.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — The passport system is a human-created institutional invention.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — No biological structure or inspiration.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not energy-dependent as an abstract artifact.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not part of any structural framework.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Observable in form, but observability is not intrinsic to its conceptual identity.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists across media; its identity is symbolic and institutional.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires institutional enforcement or user action to function.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — It is a purpose-built construct to regulate identity and mobility across political boundaries.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Included — Grants or restricts access, mobility, and legal standing.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Does not itself interpret or compute logic.
feedback.State-Transforming: Included — Alters one’s legal travel status and recognition.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Requires human presentation and inspection in standard use.
feedback.System-integrated: Included — Embedded in intergovernmental and bureaucratic systems of control and identity.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot function without institutional interpretation or validation.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — While important, it is not indispensable to global systems as a class.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Encodes identity, citizenship, and legitimacy through visual and textual representation.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Conveys critical identity and legal information to institutions.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Subject to standardized formatting and legal rules (e.g., ICAO standards).
feedback.Compositional: Included — Structured into discrete, semantically meaningful fields (name, number, issuing authority, etc.).
feedback.Normative: Included — Defines criteria for eligibility, travel rights, and civic status.
feedback.Meta: Included — Functions as documentation about the legal identity of the bearer.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Defined by explicit issuance and expiration windows; time-bounded by design.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Passports increasingly exist in virtual databases and biometric systems.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Has no standalone material identity; exists only via collective institutional recognition.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Defined, issued, and validated by state actors and treaties.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Encodes national, personal, and legal identity directly.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Heavily governed by international law and national policy.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Affects labor access, taxation, and international economic mobility.
feedback.Politicised: Included — A reflection of sovereignty, nationality, and geopolitical tensions.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Used in ceremonial moments such as border crossings and state travel rites.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises questions of fairness, statelessness, and human mobility rights.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the passport as a symbolic, institutional, and socially significant construct, not as a paper booklet. Its meaning, function, and constraints are defined entirely through law, policy, and identity systems. The inclusion of design and time-bound traits reflects the passport's engineered role in regulating temporally valid identity within political contexts.
